# Independent audit: exponential floor and uniform defect-rate kernel

Audited in full:

* `candidate 942ae5a91bb1a792`;
* `candidate d3b1d852e0e3ae4b`.

**Result: PASS, with their stated hypotheses and scope.** No repair is required. The proof of the rate-weighted flux should be read via its stated monomial-first argument; that argument completely avoids reliance on the optional cutoff discussion. The actual triangle calibration in Section 5 below confirms the direction of the kernel and all normalizations.

## 1. The exponential floor is genuinely pointwise

The assumed SAME separator tests every globally finite nonnegative convex physical potential, with continuous nonnegative normal factors. On a fixed positive neighborhood, -log L_j is finite convex. Its positive-part truncation has a globally finite convex extension agreeing on the current body, obtained from bounded subgradients on a slightly larger compact neighborhood. The bound need not be uniform in j because the inequality is tested separately at each j.

With ell_j=-log L_j and a_j=beta_j/lambda_j+C, the test Phi=(ell_j-a_j)_+ obeys Xi_j>=lambda_j Phi on its support. The two integral inequalities consequently force Phi=0 almost everywhere for surface measure. Continuity and full support of surface measure on the boundary of each positive convex fiber make this pointwise there. Concavity of L_j gives the same lower bound in every fiber, and then on their canonical hull. Thus the exponential floor and the common compact rate interval follow without reciprocal uniform integrability or a pointwise assumption on W_j.

This argument does require the stated positive-fiber framework, actual all-convex separator, and pointwise |R_j|<=C lambda_j. A mere bounded-test weak error would not suffice for this j-dependent potential.

## 2. The scale-resolved perspective tests and limit order

For g finite, nonnegative, convex and nondecreasing on [0,infinity), k(s)=s_+g(lambda s_+) is convex and nondecreasing. The perspective a k(log(a/b)-T) has positive-semidefinite Hessian on every smooth branch, with scalar coefficient k'+k''>=0. The monotonicity in a and the reverse monotonicity in b justify substitution of convex f and concave L_j. The corner contributions have the correct nonnegative derivative jumps.

On the compact rate interval g is Lipschitz. With s=ell_{j,+}, t=(s-c)_+, the exact difference decomposition is

    t g(lambda t)-s g(lambda s)+(s-t)g(0)
      =t[g(lambda t)-g(lambda s)]
                    -(s-t)[g(lambda s)-g(0)].

Both terms have absolute value bounded by a constant times lambda c s. The same bound, together with the bounded rate, controls the logarithmic quadratic contribution. Therefore the stated fixed-T limit is justified by the uniform surface logarithm mass, with no unproved second-log uniform integrability. Only after this limit does T tend to infinity. The ordinary tail then vanishes by ordinary boundary-log integrability.

The retained measures satisfy 0<=ahat<=bhat and q=pi_*(r bhat). The resulting test family is exactly the stated nonnegative-convex physical, nonnegative normal, and nonnegative-convex-nondecreasing rate family. It does not imply a pointwise cap-load inequality or arbitrary rate disintegration. The factorization r(r-t)_+=(r-t)_+^2+t(r-t)_+ verifies the upper-rate-tail corollary.

Independently reran `supporting computation verify_scale_resolved_log_defect_audit_defect_transport.py`: **3,816 exact checks PASS**.

## 3. Joint labeled inverse rates and the monomial-first Gauss--Green proof

The current inverse measures nu_ij have uniformly bounded total mass from the positive marked-value floor. Their finite labels, convergent affine planes/continuous gradients, and the common compact rate interval allow joint compactness with the ACTUAL rate coordinate. On {L>0}, reciprocal densities stay locally bounded and r_j tends uniformly to zero; thus the ordinary part has rate zero. The remaining positive measure is exactly the rate-resolved old boundary defect, supported on A_i=L=0. Labels of vanishing sigma_i carry vanishing inverse mass and cause no hidden residual.

For an integer m>=1 put F_j=ell_{j,+}r_j^m. It is Lipschitz for each fixed j. Its weak continuous gradient is exactly

    grad_X F_j=-(m+1)r_j^m grad_X log L_j.

In this display the indicator 1_(L_j<1) has been omitted LEGITIMATELY: r_j^m=0 everywhere L_j>=1. Hence neither a moving L_j=1 level nor an ordinary L=1 plateau creates a cutoff term. At finite-PL creases F_j remains continuous and locally Lipschitz, so its weak first derivative is its a.e. derivative, with no hypersurface measure.

Gauss--Green with a C1 physical test therefore gives the two actual joint measure terms in the root proof. The boundary term converges by compact rate convergence. The bulk term tends to zero: r_j tends to zero locally off the zero set, F_j is bounded by a constant times ell_{j,+}, and the BULK logarithms are uniformly integrable. The last term passes directly through the joint labeled measures because r^m is continuous and bounded. This proves

    -int phi n r^m d bhat
          =M(m+1) sum_i c_i int phi r^m d zetahat_i.

For m=0 this is exactly the independently audited unweighted defect-flux identity; no new cutoff proof is needed. Linear combinations prove the polynomial case. Approximate a C1 g and its derivative uniformly on a common compact interval (approximate g' by polynomials and integrate); bounded masses then prove the full C1 statement. Physical C1 test density permits continuous physical tests afterward.

This proof makes no normal/source identification: the right side has physical position and source-gradient labels; the left side retains the actual surface normal. A normal-dependent test cannot be inserted into the right side by fiat.

## 4. Positive radial weighting and kernel uniqueness

For fixed fiber inball centers g_z, h=n.(X-g_z)>=r_b>0 on the limiting boundary normal bundle. On each inverse defect row, A_i(z,X)=0 gives

    c_i.(X-g_z)=-A_i(z,g_z).

Each A_i(z,g_z) is positive because A_i>=L and L is positive at the finitely many interior centers. It is uniformly bounded by the convergent finite plane coefficients. Thus the radial identity produces two POSITIVE finite measures

    B=pi_(w,r)*(h bhat),
    V=M sum_i A_i(z,g_z) zetahat_i,

with int phi r^m dV=(m+1)^(-1) int phi r^m dB for all m>=0. Fiberwise choices of g_z are legitimate in this flux calculation even if their graph is not affine; this is not a claim that h is an admissible convex variation.

At rate R, the uniform law U_R on [0,R], with U_0=delta_0, has precisely moments R^m/(m+1). Applying that kernel to B therefore yields all the same moments as V. Polynomials in the compact rate coordinate, tensored with continuous physical functions, are uniformly dense in the continuous product space. This proves equality of the measures, not just equality of their rate marginals.

It follows that the positive-rate marginal of V has the stated nonincreasing density and no positive-rate atoms. Its only possible rate atom is zero, of mass B(rate=0). The positive lower source-plane weights imply that each individual zetahat_i also has no atom at a fixed positive rate. None of this excludes arbitrary tangential concentration or a rate-zero defect. Neither the radial nor source-plane weights may be removed from the positive kernel statement.

## 5. Exact actual truncated-triangle calibration

This is an ACTUAL convex-body/contact-row sequence, not an asserted physical stationary sequence. It generalizes the archived truncation with eta=2^(-m).

Fix gamma>0 and R>0. For integers m sufficiently large set

    a=1/m, eta=exp(-gamma m), b=a-eta,
    K_m={x,y>=0: a<=t=x+y<=1},
    ell_m=t-b=t-a+eta,
    L_m=c_m ell_m,
    lambda_m=R/(gamma m).

Choose c_m by mean_(K_m) log L_m=0. The coordinates

    (t,r) -> (rt,(1-r)t),  0<=r<=1,

have Jacobian t. Hence V_m=(1-a^2)/2 and

    Z_m=int_Km 1/ell_m dm
        =1-a+b log[(1-a+eta)/eta] -> 1+gamma.

The log primitive, with v=t-b, is

    v^2 log v/2-v^2/4+b(v log v-v).

It gives int_Km log ell_m dm -> -1/4 and therefore c_m -> c=exp(1/2). The exact probability row

    rho_m=dm/(Z_m ell_m)

has source Y_m equal to its mean and L_m(Y_m)=c_m V_m/Z_m. Consequently

    (1/L_m(Y_m))rho_m=dm/(V_m L_m),
    bar_rho_m=dm/V_m.

Thus this is one affine parameter and one genuine contact row. If

    I_m=int_a^1 t^2/(t-b) dt,

then Y_m=(I_m/(2Z_m),I_m/(2Z_m)), I_m->1/2, so

    Y_m -> (1/[4(1+gamma)],1/[4(1+gamma)]),
    L_m(Y_m) -> c/[2(1+gamma)]>0.

The sources have a uniform own-fiber ball and the parameters have uniform maxima. The limiting source is not deepest in the triangle: its small-side t-cap has fraction 1/[4(1+gamma)^2], strictly below 4/9. This limitation is essential.

The bottom edge has normal n0=-(1,1)/sqrt(2), length sqrt(2)/m, and constant negative logarithm gamma m-log c_m. Its rate tends to R. All other edges have uniformly integrable logarithms, so the rate-resolved surface defect is

    bhat=sqrt(2) gamma delta_(n0,0,R).                (A)

For the inverse measure use the EXACT split

    t/(t-b)=1+b/(t-b).

The first term gives the ordinary limiting density dm/t at rate zero. In the second put

    q=-log[c_m(t-b)]/(gamma m).

Then dt/(t-b)=-gamma m dq. Since m b->1, its coefficient tends to gamma/c after division by c_m. The q-range tends to [0,1]; any part with q<0 has vanishing mass. For each fixed q>0 the physical point tends to the vertex 0, and its actual rate is Rq. Dominated convergence on this finite q interval proves the full joint weak limit. With V_m->1/2,

    zetahat=(2 gamma/c) delta_0(dw) U_R(ds).          (B)

Thus the inverse defect rates really are UNIFORM on [0,R], not concentrated at the surface rate R. For the archived eta=2^(-m), take gamma=log 2 and lambda_m=R/(m log 2).

To verify every positive radial normalization, choose the fixed limiting inball center g=(1/3,1/3), which is also an interior center for K_m for all large m. At the defect point,

    h=n0.(0-g)=2/(3sqrt(2)),
    A(g)=2c/3,  M=1/2.

Equations (A)--(B) give

    B=(2 gamma/3) delta_0(dw) delta_R(ds),
    V=(2 gamma/3) delta_0(dw) U_R(ds).

The m-th moment of the latter is exactly 1/(m+1) times the former. The vector sign is also correct: -n0 sqrt(2)gamma=gamma(1,1)=M c(1,1)(2gamma/c).

The calibration requires only the bounded-rate and contact-row hypotheses for the flux/kernel statement. It makes no claim that the separator-derived bound R<=beta holds for this family or that its caps obey the physical stress. One may choose R arbitrarily small if a bounded rate interval is desired; actual stationarity is still not asserted.

The independent checker `supporting computation verify_uniform_defect_rate_kernel_audit_slab_recovery.py` verifies the exact primitives, contact-row identities, rate Jacobian, positive radial/vector factors, and moment-kernel formulas. The limit and density conclusions are proved above, not inferred from floating-point approximations.
